applicability.description: The repository owns an automated test, validation, verification, or policy-checking surface.

requirements.statement: Canonical suites and their support assets are physically owned by the capability or behavior they verify; repository-native equivalent structures are permitted.
Feature records remain the canonical history and each active numbered scenario maps to exactly one executable owner and evidence kind.
Canonical suites are discovered recursively as normalized repository-relative identities in ordinal order, and ambiguous, unsafe, linked, duplicate, or empty discovery fails closed.
Shared test infrastructure contains only generic discovery, execution, result, evidence, or cleanup mechanics and does not own capability-specific assertions.
Canonical suites execute in separate processes unless reviewed repository-native evidence proves an equivalent isolation boundary.
Mutable fixtures, mocks, repositories, environment state, and temporary roots are capability-local and freshly reset for each case; shared immutable fixtures have explicit owners and byte identity.

conforming: Reviewed topology evidence identifies canonical suites, support assets, discovery order, and process boundaries.
Reviewed traceability evidence maps every active numbered scenario to one executable owner and evidence kind.
Focused execution evidence demonstrates fixture reset, cleanup, and isolation for representative mutable boundaries.
notApplicable: Reviewed repository evidence proves that no automated test, validation, verification, or policy-checking surface exists.
The review identifies the repository scope and explains why adding such a surface is outside the repository's current authority.
